question: Naši predkovia mali na oblohe dve krásne svetlá: Zorničku, ktorá svieti nad ránom, a Večernicu, ktorá svieti po západe slnka. V skutočnosti ide o jedno a to isté nebeské teleso. Ktoré?

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak knows Zornička from fairy tales and songs and assumes it is a star. It turns out to be a planet, and the same body as the 'other' star of the evening. The player can reason it out because it is the brightest point in the sky after the Moon.
extra.verification_notes: Venus is traditionally both the morning star (Zornička) and evening star (Večernica); the Slovak article at startitup.sk (https://www.startitup.sk/?p=1028123) treats it that way and I found no contradicting source.

explanation: Venuša obieha bližšie k Slnku ako Zem, preto ju nikdy neuvidíme o polnoci, len nízko nad obzorom ráno alebo večer. Po Mesiaci je to najjasnejší objekt nočnej oblohy.

question: Veľký voz pozná na oblohe takmer každý, no v skutočnosti to nie je samostatné súhvezdie. Je len časťou väčšieho súhvezdia. Ktorého?
source_excerpt: The Big Dipper is an asterism, not a constellation, and forms part of Ursa Major.

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak child learns to find 'Veľký voz' and assumes it is a constellation in its own right. In fact it is only the back and tail of a much larger bear, which most people have never traced. Many players can reason their way to the answer from the half-remembered name.
extra.verification_notes: The Big Dipper/Plough is an asterism within the IAU constellation Ursa Major (Veľká medvedica), per https://www.astronomy.com/observing/explore-the-big-dipper-this-winter/

explanation: Sedem hviezd Veľkého voza tvorí chrbát a chvost Veľkej medvedice. Oj voza je v skutočnosti medvedí chvost, aj keď skutočné medvede majú chvost len maličký.
